summary.title: HopChain: Multi-Hop Data Synthesis for Generalizable Vision-Language Reasoning

details: VLM long chain-of-thought reasoning fails in diverse, compounding ways (perception, reasoning, knowledge, hallucination errors) because existing vision-language RLVR data rarely requires visual evidence at every step, leaving these weaknesses unexposed during training.

HopChain: a scalable pipeline that synthesizes multi-hop vision-language RLVR queries from real images, where each query is a logically dependent chain of instance-grounded hops (earlier hops establish the instances/sets/conditions needed by later hops) terminating in a single unambiguous number for verifiable reward.

Formalized hop structure: queries must combine 'perception-level hops' (alternating single-object vs. multi-object/relational perception) with 'instance-chain hops' (A -> B -> C dependency), so language-only shortcuts are blocked and visual re-grounding is forced at every step.

Pipeline: VLM category identification -> SAM3 instance segmentation -> VLM multi-hop query generation over 3-6 instance combinations -> human-in-the-loop ground-truth annotation plus difficulty calibration.

Image filtering favoring perceptually hard images (occlusion, dense objects, unusual poses, fine-grained distinctions); two-stage filter using Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Thinking plus an SFT-distilled Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Thinking screener
Query generation by Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Thinking given the image and instance crops; constraints forbid referencing masks/boxes/patches and require answerability from the original image alone

Stage 4: four annotators independently solve each query; retained only if all four agree on the final number and no ambiguity reported; queries with 100% accuracy under a weaker model (8 samples) removed as too easy
Final yield ~6k-8k multi-hop RLVR samples per model, mixed with a similar amount of math RLVR data as the original RLVR data
Qwen3.5-35B-A3B and Qwen3.5-397B-A17B, starting from an internal pre-final SFT checkpoint
SAPO (soft adaptive policy optimization, temperature-controlled soft gate instead of hard clipping), lr 2e-6, binary correctness reward
35B: 16 rollouts x 256 queries, mini-batch 64, 1000 steps; 397B: mini-batch 128, 800 steps
Three settings: Before RLVR (SFT only), RLVR w/o Multi-Hop (original data only), RLVR w/ Multi-Hop (original + synthesized data)

24 benchmarks in four families: STEM/puzzle (MathVision, MMMU/MMMU-Pro, BabyVision, ZeroBench, EMMA, LogicVista), general VQA (MMBench, RealWorldQA, MMStar, HallusionBench, AI2D, ERQA), text/document (CharXiv, DocVQA, InfoVQA), video (Video-MME, Video-MMMU, MVBench, LVBench, MLVU, MMVU)
Hop-structure ablation on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B: full multi-hop vs. half-multi-hop (latter half of chain) vs. single hop (final hop only), evaluated on five representative benchmarks
Accuracy binned by response token length on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B
Query-level pass@k style difficulty histogram (8 samples per query) for both model scales
Human error-type labeling of 20 random incorrect responses per benchmark for the baseline, plus error types of cases corrected by multi-hop training

key_findings.finding: Adding benchmark-agnostic HopChain multi-hop data to RLVR yields broad gains across benchmark families and model scales.
key_findings.evidence: 20 of 24 benchmarks improve over RLVR on original data alone for both Qwen3.5-35B-A3B and Qwen3.5-397B-A17B; e.g. 35B CharXiv 69.0->73.1, EMMA(mini) 53.0->58.0, MathVision 73.7->76.1; 397B BabyVision 28.6->32.2, ZeroBench 4->8, Video-MME 78.3->80.4. Gains include 5/6 video benchmarks despite image-only training data.

key_findings.finding: Preserving the full logically dependent hop chain is essential; truncating it degrades transfer.
key_findings.evidence: On Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, average over MathVision, MMMU-Pro, RealWorldQA, ERQA, VideoMMMU drops from 70.4 (full multi-hop) to 66.7 (latter-half chain) to 64.3 (final hop only), with the same ordering on every one of the five benchmarks.

key_findings.finding: The benefit is concentrated in long-CoT reasoning, growing with response length.
key_findings.evidence: Binning Qwen3.5-397B-A17B benchmark responses by token count, the accuracy advantage of RLVR w/ Multi-Hop persists across bins and is largest in the ultra-long-response regime, exceeding 50 accuracy points there.

key_findings.finding: Long-CoT VLM failures are diverse rather than a single mode, and multi-hop training corrects them broadly rather than patching one type.
key_findings.evidence: Human annotation of baseline errors shows perception errors largest, followed by reasoning, plus knowledge and hallucination; the error-type distribution of cases corrected after adding multi-hop data closely mirrors the baseline distribution, with subtype gains spanning chart/text misreads, object misidentification, spatial/counting, logic, math, temporal and causal errors.

key_findings.finding: The synthesized data spans a usable difficulty range for both small and large models.
key_findings.evidence: Sampling 8 responses per multi-hop query, over half of queries fall in the partially-correct regime (1/8-7/8) for both Qwen3.5-35B-A3B and Qwen3.5-397B-A17B, with mass spread across success buckets rather than collapsing to 0/8 or 8/8.
